items.headline: New AI tool maps the hidden universe of small molecules
items.excerpt: A new AI model charts the vast, largely uncatalogued space of small molecules, giving chemists and metabolomics researchers a way to identify compounds that current reference libraries miss.

items.headline: Hot subdwarfs come into focus as AI scans thousands of stars in Gaia data
items.excerpt: A machine-learning pipeline sifted Gaia's catalogue to pull thousands of hot subdwarf stars out of the noise, sharply expanding a sample that had been painstakingly assembled by hand.

items.headline: Explainable AI could help turn hidden data patterns into testable scientific hypotheses
items.excerpt: Researchers argue that explainable-AI methods can be repurposed as a discovery engine: instead of only justifying predictions, the explanations become candidate hypotheses scientists can go and test in the lab.

items.headline: Brain activity patterns could help sharpen LLM deductive reasoning
items.excerpt: A team used human brain-activity recordings during deductive reasoning tasks as a training signal, nudging large language models toward more human-like inference.

items.headline: AI may help identify breast cancers missed by mammograms, but clinical benefit remains uncertain
items.excerpt: A new evidence review finds AI readers do surface cancers human screeners miss, while cautioning that better detection has not yet been shown to translate into better patient outcomes.

items.headline: AI models show promising results in ICU mortality predictions
items.excerpt: Machine-learning models trained on intensive-care records outperformed the standard severity scores clinicians rely on for predicting ICU mortality.

items.headline: People affected by cancer need a stronger voice in shaping generative AI for oncology, review finds
items.excerpt: A scoping review of 2,441 records found only 32 studies that asked cancer patients, survivors and caregivers how they feel about generative AI in their care, published in the European Journal of Cancer.

items.headline: Transfer learning for genomic prediction in underrepresented populations
items.excerpt: Google Research describes a transfer-learning approach that carries polygenic prediction power from data-rich cohorts into populations that genomics studies have historically left out.

items.headline: Planetary prediction engine: Automating global models via Earth AI
items.excerpt: Google's Earth AI stack automates the construction of global geospatial models, letting researchers stand up planet-scale predictions of environmental variables without hand-built pipelines.

items.headline: Live from ICM 2026: What Is Math For in the Age of AI?
items.excerpt: A live recording from the International Congress of Mathematicians asks what mathematicians actually value about doing mathematics, now that AI systems can produce proofs.

items.headline: In an Age of AI, a Physicist Seeks What Endures
items.excerpt: Yale physics chair Sarah Demers on where large language models can genuinely help particle physics and where she thinks they erode the craft of the field.

items.headline: AI dominates the 4th International Congress of Basic Science in Beijing
items.excerpt: Subir Sarkar reports from Beijing, where AI was the dominant theme among more than 800 delegates debating how machine learning is reshaping basic physics, math and life science.

items.headline: Improved QLEDs with machine learning
items.excerpt: Machine learning identified solvent formulations that produce highly homogeneous quantum-dot films, improving QLED performance without trial-and-error chemistry.

items.headline: The Attention Deficit of AI Revealed
items.excerpt: A PNAS Nexus study ran leading LLMs through the Stroop test and found they have limited executive control of attention — a gap the authors say is architectural, not just a memory problem.

items.headline: The hard parts of AI-assisted science
items.excerpt: Ai2 researchers lay out five unsolved problems in AI-assisted science: keeping agents steerable as a project evolves, deciding what to delegate, and stopping AI from amplifying methodological flaws.

items.headline: Piloting the world's first double-blind AI evaluations
items.excerpt: DeepMind describes a pilot bringing double-blind methodology — long standard in clinical and behavioural science — to AI model evaluation, so neither evaluators nor developers know which system they are scoring.
